result.title: EpiSEM-Bench: Evaluating Safety and Evidence Recovery in LLM Agents under Missing Evidence
result.summary: Tool-using language model agents rely on environmental facts to decide whether an action is permitted. When a tool response omits a safety-relevant fact, an agent may carry out a prohibited action even though the user request is benign and every returned statement is true. We introduce \bench{}, an executable benchmark for evaluating unsafe execution, safety boundaries, and evidence recovery in LLM agents under missing evidence. It contains 300 matched unsafe/safe task pairs across six domains. By systematically suppressing critical facts, the benchmark measures unsafe execution under critical evidence omission and determines the minimum observed failure cardinality, including failures with full evidence and cases with no observed failure after exhaustive testing. An independent audit tool tests whether agents seek missing facts and then withhold prohibited actions while completing permissible tasks. The benchmark reveals substantial variation across the ten models in omission robustness, evidence acquisition, and appropriate action. Resistance to missing evidence does not necessarily translate into useful recovery. Recovery access reduces unsafe execution for all ten models, but agents differ in whether they actively obtain the missing facts and use them to act appropriately in both worlds.

AI.brief_summary: 论文提出 EpiSEM-Bench：一个可执行基准，用 300 组配对的「安全/不安全」任务、跨六个领域系统性隐藏关键事实，测量 LLM agent 在证据缺失下的不安全执行、是否能主动查找缺失证据，以及拿到证据后能否正确使用。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「是否主动获取缺失事实、并据其改变行动」的评测与 LVR 中视觉证据筛选、LOOK/证据获取及其是否被答案真正使用的因果核查问题相通，可供核查这一任务形式如何迁移到视觉证据缺失场景；但对象是工具型文本 agent 的安全合规，而非多模态推理本身。
